proposals.reasoning: The core defect is real and worse than the proposer measured. On my own DGP (6 states, 3 onset cohorts, i=coh, cluster(state), permexact over 90 assignments) adding coarsecohortcontrols(c.cohbase) leaves e(b) BITWISE identical at +1.d19927ea8a230X+000 while moving e(perm_p_att) from .0222222 (the exact floor 2/90) to .6444444 and e(perm_sd_att) from 0.6897432 to 3.5018705 - a 5.08x null-SD inflation, above the proposal's claimed 3-4x. The blast-radius claim is verified to a stronger standard than the proposer used: I dumped every e() scalar and every matrix cell at %21x on both builds in separate Stata launches and diffed as strings; 0 of 1229 lines differ across the six surviving arms, including the safety(off) identity (invariant 2) and the cluster()==i geometry control (invariant 1). I also closed the proposer's Open Question 3: the inertness premise holds on customvce(cluster), poisson, unconditionalse, esfixedbaseperiod and aweights - controls(cohbase) and fe(cohbase) leave e(b) bitwise identical on all five (run1.log arms B/C/D/E/F). The caution prints exactly once (the shell's re-run of wooldid_validate is under qui). What fails is the predicate and the message. The '#' tokenizer screens interaction factors, so it refuses live terms by exactly the criterion the proposal uses to exempt interactivecontrols(); gegen tag() drops missing rows, so it screens terms whose removal changes e(sample); and the design-sample evaluation produces a measured false negative (run4_fn.do: xfn = cohbase except 999 on three markout-dead rows -> tag(coh xfn)=6 on the design sample so the screen is SILENT, tag=3 on the estimation sample so the term is exactly inert, e(b) bitwise identical +1.c722552b26148X+000 with N=57 in both arms, while e(perm_sd_att) moves 0.740148297358301 -> 0.663963823146380, -10.3%, and the permutation band moves from [-1.2311175, 1.4561430] to [-1.1304840, 1.4062481]). That false negative is a moderate-realism confirmation of the proposer's own Open Question 3 rather than a new blind spot; a second unmeasured route is Q4 controls(xmiss) (whole cohort missing, tag=2!=3), which ran silently on the patched build. Note that the refusal on controls(xscat) is itself defensible - the term is inert given the sample and live in the reps - so F3 falsifies the advice sentence and the cert invariant, not the screen's direction. Only the interaction tokenizer is a genuine false positive on realistic input, and it is blocking.

mech: LAT = contreat()+lattice(). A lattice gives each treated (cell x bin) piece its own intercept and its own dose slope. The proposal's story — a piece with n <= 1+contreatpoly observations is fitted exactly, residuals identically zero, so every residual-based variance estimator is blind where the iid bread says variance is huge, and Stata's ereturn-post screen zeroes the whole e(V) — is right about the fixture but WRONG as a general predicate, and I falsified it by measurement. A piece with n=2 and only ONE distinct dose value has its slope dropped for collinearity, so it carries 1 free parameter for 2 observations and its residuals are NOT zero. The correct saturation predicate is n <= 1 + min(poly, nd-1), which needs a nunique() pass, not the count() pass the proposal priced. Separately, the saturated-piece COUNT does not order the outcomes: measured on 11 (fixture x lattice) combinations on the patched build, h20+lattice(all 3) dies at 1.3% saturated pieces and h40+lattice(all 6) dies at 0.9%, while a discrete-dose 40-unit panel at lattice(all 5) survives at 3.8% with a healthy e(V) and ame se .0542 (t 6.13). Verified separately: the shipped all-zero-covariance caution really does blame clustering on runs that clustered nothing — it fires with the false text on 14 of my 24 configurations. FALSIFIED by a cry-wolf case. r02b.log arm L: 12 states x 40 units x 20 years, dose a UNIT-LEVEL DISCRETE level in {1..10} (a tier, count or bracket — an ordinary applied dose), lattice(all 5) robust. L3 FIRES ('into 390 cell-by-bin pieces, and 15 of them hold 2 or fewer observations ... the 30 treated observation(s) in them have residuals of zero ... the analytic standard errors ... can be far smaller than the estimates' sampling variability, and the estimation command may return an all-zero covariance instead'), and the run is FINE: e(V) posted (e(wdid_vcvstate)=analytic-diagonal), no all-zero caution anywhere, ame = .33226979, se = .05418031, t = 6.13, p = 0.000 (truth .4; the no-lattice control arm M gives ame .42644296, se .01027381). This is the same cry-wolf standard the proposer used to kill L2.

The caution's own mechanism sentence, 'the `lsobs' treated observation(s) in them have residuals of zero'. FALSE for 30 of 30 flagged observations on arm L. The offline census in the same log shows all 15 saturated pieces there have n=2 with exactly ONE distinct dose value: 'CENSUS disc-all5: saturated(n<=2)=15 ... treated obs in saturated pieces=30 ... of those, obs in one-distinct-dose pieces=30'. A piece with one distinct dose value has its slope dropped for collinearity, so it carries ONE free parameter for TWO observations and its residuals are +/- half the within-piece y gap. The exact predicate is not n <= 1+poly; it is n <= 1 + min(poly, nd-1) — which needs a nunique() pass, precisely the pass the proposal removed to reach its quoted price ('count() instead of nunique(), which does not have to hash the values').

'on the healthy one, 0 of 234 (p07b_healthy.log: minimum 7 distinct dose values per piece, median 13)'. That is a statement about lattice(all 3), not about the fixture. Measured on the same 40-unit-per-state healthy panel at lattice(all 6): 467 pieces, 4 saturated, 7 treated observations — and the covariance is ALL-ZERO, no e(V) posted, att and ame both se-less (r03_l3b.log arm L3B-4, confirmed on the patched build as r02_crywolf_partial.log arm C, hasV=0).

The saturated-piece count does not order the outcomes at all. A design dies at 0.9% and survives at 3.8%.

'This is the same cost class the package has already accepted, on a strictly narrower set of runs.' FALSE. R1's detect screen runs on clustered contreat runs; L3 runs on lattice contreat runs. proposals.reasoning: The core statistics are correct and I verified them three independent ways. (1) Closed form + my own 200k-draw ideal-model MC (a_ideal.py) reproduces their PART A size table exactly (k=3,nu=15: 0.0784; k=4: 0.1034; k=6: 0.1840), their Leg C coverage (0.9107->0.9498 at k=3,nu=15; 0.8855->0.9504 at k=4; unchanged at k=1), and their mdt ratios (ship 0.8893 -> +A 0.9078 -> +A+B 1.0008). The Anderson step-down pivot is genuinely exact and Q is genuinely theta-invariant. Leg B's rescale (c2hat/c2true ~ nu/chi2(nu-k+1)) is the standard Wishart result and the median-unbiasing is right. (2) Live pinned-vs-patched at %21x reproduces the closed-form mdt multipliers to 6 decimals on my own panel, and the gate-off arms (iid, robust, bootstrap, poisson) are bit-identical. (3) Re-analysing their own stored per-replication W (mc_null/powS/powP.csv) reproduces their headline MC table exactly: size 0.0840->0.0560, power 0.7600->0.6960 at the shipped mdt80 and 0.8720->0.8040 at the patched one, empirical 95th percentile of W 11.9320 against their computed cutoff 11.8057. So the mechanism ships. What does not ship as written is the document: it omits an edit its own tested build contains (the live slope line), its no-oracle test #1 is falsified on 7 of 20 draws, its se multiplier is presented as a constant when it is data-dependent, its blast radius is quoted at one (k, G) cell when the surface runs to x18.5, and it applies a Hotelling scaling to a generalized-inversed block where the distribution theory does not hold. The PS-64 divergence is real and correctly disclosed (e(joint_horiz) bit-identical, e(roth_prep_att) moved; p1 ARM_G), and I found no other consumer of roth_* anywhere in the ado, so option (A) is containable. Note the one arm that shows sub-1e-12 movement outside the gate, p3 H1 (unconditionalse cluster(st)): roth_W rel 1.3e-13, roth_slope rel 2.0e-13, roth_nissize rel 6.6e-15. The proposer's own 'grep -c "lie wholly inside a single" run2_pf.log returns 3' is a count over C5, C6 and C7 - two bootstrap runs and one analytic run - so he saw it fire under bootstrap and read the count without reading the text.

'Exactly the arms A1 shows are broken, and no others.' False in both directions. FALSE NEGATIVE: customvce(robust) never reaches the observation branch, because ado:4667 makes customvce() incompatible with robust and cluster(), so the local `robust' is necessarily empty there. Measured on a 25-state panel with i=cohort and cohort 1 holding one state: `robust' prints '10 of 21 ... lie wholly inside a single observation' and posts e(gt_ncontained)=10; `customvce(robust)' prints nothing and posts nothing - on output that agrees to 5.7e-14 relative on estimate, 1.2e-13 on se and 3.4e-12 on p, i.e. the same numbers to within the project's 1e-10 indifference threshold. 'fastnose: the help says the regression's own VCE is intact under it, so GTE-1's floor applies and GTE-4 is skipped by its fastnose gate. My control arm for it errored r(459), so this is asserted from the code, not measured.' Measured, and the gate is wrong. `cluster(state) gteffects' and `cluster(state) gteffects fastnose' return BIT-IDENTICAL e(gteffects) - 21 rows, every one of the 15 columns, rows=21 semiss=0 setiny=0 minse=1.759e-01 maxse=7.072e-01 minp=8.057e-13 - and only the first is disclosed. sthlp:1151 calls gteffects 'the one inference surface that survives fast mode', so the gate silences the disclosure in the mode where the cell table is the only inference the run produces. The same gate also silences it under plain permute(), which runs the observed fit in fast-nose mode: permute(shuffle) gives gt_ndegen=6 with e(gt_ncontained) ABSENT, while permute(shuffle) permanalyticse and permute(shuffle) permtstat on the identical data give e(gt_ncontained)=30.

'Multi-way cluster(): GTE-4 loops the cluster variables and keeps the largest count. Not measured.' Measured. The max() aggregation means any cluster variable that is constant within a cohort-by-relative-period cell forces 100% containment - and the time variable is constant within such a cell BY CONSTRUCTION. On 60 states / 3 cohorts of 15 / 12 years, cluster(state year) and cluster(year state) both print '18 of 18 e(gteffects) cell(s) lie wholly inside a single cluster' although every cell holds 15 distinct states; cluster(state) on the same data is silent with cell se 0.259-0.480. In that run reghdfe's CGM collapses to N_clust=12 and the cell SEs come back missing anyway, so the count is not harmful there - but the wording is: the caution says the columns are 'understated by a design-dependent factor' when they are in fact missing. customvce(cluster state year) on the same data prints '18 of 18' while every cell carries an ordinary se of 0.026-0.153.

'The right predicate already exists in the file ... wooldid_amescreen, mode(detect) ... It is gated at ado:1534 to "`contreat'" != "".' The proposal reuses R1's predicate but silently changes R1's gate. R1 is gated off under impvalues and under unconditionalse as well as fastnose ('different estimand; excluded from suppression by design'); GTE-4 keeps only the fastnose exclusion. Honest list of what I did NOT test.

1. COST. I did not re-measure the 2,000,000-row timings. The proposal's 0.238 s / 0.128 s figures are taken on trust; note the GTE-4 cost table measures the cluster branch on one design while the wdrepmode gate is justified by a print count that cannot test it (replications are quiet - measured).
2. bootdisplay(bca) and the delete-one-cluster jackknife path with gteffects. Only percentile, bc, wald, bayes and boottstat were run.
3. The plain-bootstrap branch where the cell rewiring FAILS - a failed 'cap confirm matrix `cell'_gt' at ado:6611, or the wdb_cellkeydup path at ado:9157. That is the one bootstrap branch where e(gteffects) keeps ANALYTIC se/p/ci under a bootstrap header, so GTE-1's scrub would be displayed while GTE-2's caution is gated off. I could not construct it.
4. subgroups() crossed with degenerate cells (I ran subgroups only on the proposer's clean C3 arm, via his logs).
5. contreat()/lattice() - gteffects is refused with contreat() at ado:4695, so the surfaces cannot interact; I did not test the refusal itself.
6. fweights: wooldid refuses them outright ('Error: wooldid does not accept fweights'), so GTE-4's weight branch only ever needs pweight. The [fw] token in the syntax line at ado:555 is vestigial; I did not chase it.
7. A design where gtcontain (a count of DATA cells) exceeds gtn (a count of COEFFICIENT rows), which would make the caution read 'N of M' with N > M. On all 12 arms where the screen fired the two agreed (10/21, 39/39, 109/109, 18/18, 30/30, 17/17, 6/9). Not falsified, not guaranteed.
8. GTE-1 clause (a) when est is MISSING. In Mata 'se < 1e-10*abs(.)' evaluates as 'se < .' which is TRUE for any finite se, so a cell with a missing coefficient and a finite variance would be scrubbed and counted. I could not reach it - reghdfe posts 0 for omitted coefficients, not missing - and scrubbing would arguably be right anyway. Flagged as a code-reading observation, not a measurement.
9. Multiway cluster where the CGM meat is genuinely healthy in the non-degenerate dimension. In my 60-state / 12-year design reghdfe's min-cluster rule collapsed N_clust to 12 and the cell SEs came back missing, and the cluster(state cohid) arm collapsed to N_clust=4. The one arm with ordinary SEs and a '18 of 18' caution went through customvce(cluster state year), whose own standard errors are 10x smaller than cluster(state)'s and whose e(N_clust) is empty - a pre-existing customvce pass-through oddity, not GTE's, and I did not chase it. So the multiway finding rests on the max() logic and the wording, not on a demonstrated wrong disclosure over healthy SEs.
10. Register/voice measurement of the GTE-5 prose against 2a2da17 on caps, ' - ' per 1000 words and asides - the check 5b's own closing note calls for.
11. I did not run the project's test suite, battery, baselines or prebuilt fixtures, per the brief. Every design here is freshly generated in body_env.do / body_boot.do / body_perm.do / body_mw.do.
12. The boot_*.log B5 arm is invalid (permute(standard) is not a legal mode; the base run returned rc 198 and my DUMP printed stale e() from the previous arm). It is superseded by perm_base.log / perm_pf.log and should not be cited.

What round 1 MISSED is that the fix is sufficient only for the class it was aimed at. A cluster variable that varies within a unit — two movers in forty — still fails the predicate, still triggers Variant A's r(459), and the run it refuses is within 3% of the run it permits with identical df. proposals.reasoning: The screen is cheap, it moves no reported number, and the site is right. Round 1's central falsification -- that it cries wolf on a discrete unit-level dose -- is CORRECT, and I proved it on the axis they never measured: a frozen-design MC says disc/all5's standard error is not merely posted but correctly sized. mech: OTHER / SK-FC-A. Mechanism as stated by the proposal is right: with `i` coarser than the unit and no fixed effect at or below the cluster, the permanent between-unit differences sit in the residual, and anything that moves the composition of the (i,t) cells moves the point estimate, while clustering below `i` nets that variation out of the standard error. What is wrong is the OPERATIONALISATION. Code facts I established by reading the pinned build: ado:928 sets `_i` = `i` on treated rows, so the treatment terms are i.`_i'#i.`_t'#i.targetflag — (i-level x relative-period). Coarsening `i` changes the MODEL (fewer treatment parameters), not merely the cell weights; that is why i=coh+fe(u) is not equal to i=u on a ragged panel (rev1 R5b r2 .99467 vs .99581). ado:1476 puts fe() inside reghdfe's absorb(); ado:1485 (the regress path used by unconditionalse/customvce) splices `fe' in RAW, so fe(state) there is a LINEAR state term. ado:1141 makes ccc_absorb() into i.`_i'#i.`_t'#c.(vars) — cell slopes, never unit effects. SEPARATE PACKAGE DEFECT found while probing, independent of both proposals and worth its own ticket: `wooldid y coh t ttre, att unconditionalse cluster(state) fe(state)` on my selective-attrition panel returns att = 0.006773106912 against a truth of 1 (r2 .0512) with no error and only the generic ado:4637 caution — and that caution's own advice ("You must specify anything in fe as controls") is wrong, because fe(i.state) works and returns 0.974232779641, identical to the reghdfe fe(state) arm to 1 ulp. customvce(cluster state) fe(state) behaves the same (0.006773106912).

falsified_claims: "Overflow is not a concern either way: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds every rescaled off-diagonal by se_k * se_j" and "V = (V :* vsc') :* vsc broadcasts instead and is arithmetically identical". FALSE. The Cauchy-Schwarz bound applies to the PRODUCT diag(vsc)V diag(vsc), not to the standalone K x K temporary `vsc' * vsc`, whose cells are vsc_k*vsc_j and obey no such bound. Measured (p6_ovf.log): V[1,1]=V[1,2]=V[2,2]=1e-320, se=0.1 -> vsc=1e159; `vsc'*vsc` gives MISSING at [1,1]; `V :* (vsc'*vsc)` (the proposed form) gives A[1,1]=MISSING and A[1,2]=MISSING; `(V :* vsc') :* vsc` gives B[1,1]=B[1,2]=.01 = se^2, the correct answer. The two forms are not arithmetically identical, and the failure is silent: a MISSING V[k,k] does not satisfy the sentinel test `V[k,k] == 0` at ado:14565, so the column escapes the -1e100 branch and e(V) ships a missing variance with no error. Exposure needs vsc > ~1.34e154 (a subnormal listwise variance beside a normal per-column se), so severity is low — but the fix is free.

Edit (5) as SPELLED is wrong code and I measured its failure. The proposal writes `sr[a] < 1e-8*ase[idx[a]]`, but in wooldid_bootsgw `ase = st_matrix(aseobsname)[1, idx']` is ALREADY subsetted to the m selected columns, so `ase[idx[a]]` indexes a 1 x m vector with an original accumulator column number. Applied literally (build patched5bad) the S1 run dies: `wooldid_bootsgw(): 3301 subscript invalid`, `_rc = 3301`. The companion `pwo[j]` should be `pwo[1, j]` as the W_obs loop above it already writes.

The failure mode of that spelling is worse than a crash. `mata: wooldid_bootsgw(...)` at ado:7129 is NOT cap-wrapped, and it runs after wooldid_bootwire has already posted the bootstrap coefficient table (e(boot_ndegse)=24, e(esband_crit_att)=32.404 are posted on the aborted run) but BEFORE wooldid_bootjnt's pairwise rewiring. The aborted run therefore leaves a MIXED e(): e(joint_att_allsgssame)=7.672e-18, e(joint_pre_att_allsgssame)=.00063753, e(pwsgs)[1,4]=7.67e-18, e(boot_tstud_pwsgs) ABSENT — against .14285714 / .46 on the correctly-spelled build. The patch leaves wooldid_bootband's n<2 refusal string false. falsified_claims: "mixed -> se(att_i), se(att_it), se(att_itime) and everything computed from the bootstrap covariance of those estimands **rise**, back toward the value the same data would give with the straddler removed." FALSIFIED unqualified at a realistic straddler count. At k = 3 in 100 units se(att_i) FALLS in 6 of 6 measurements: -16.5%, -18.6%, -20.0% (tau_straddler > tau_nesting) and -11.3%, -11.7%, -6.7% (reversed), across three independent seeds. It rises only on the straddler-heavy designs (k = 40: +16.5%, +10.6%). The direction is not a structural property of the rule.

Round 1's "SMP-3's mis-weighting is ... of the opposite sign, so whether it helps or hurts ... depends on which group carries the larger effect (reverse the taus on my design and the pinned rule would be the one landing further out)." FALSIFIED. Reversing the taus flips the SIGN of both builds' biases and leaves SMP-3 further from zero in both orderings and at both straddler counts: -0.464 -> -1.561 and +0.423 -> +1.562 at k = 40; -0.155 -> -0.601 and -0.042 -> +0.251 at k = 3. The mis-weighting does not trade one sign for another; on every design I ran it amplifies whatever bias the pinned rule already has.

"`se(att)` and every point estimate are untouched." TRUE on the plain bootstrap(standard) path (bit-identical in all 10 arms) and FALSE in the sense a user sees on the boottstat path, which SMP-3 also drives (boottstat + cluster() takes the same reid leg). At k = 3 straddlers in 100 units the reported p-value for att moves 0.400 -> 0.300 and its 95% interval moves [-.17109913, .97414421] -> [-.09520187, .96837311]; at k = 40, [1.5354021, 2.7029761] -> [1.5403477, 2.542011]. Mechanism: under boottstat each replication estimates its own analytic standard error, and re-identifying the nesting units changes that replication's parameterisation, so every column's studentized ratio moves even where its coefficient draws do not.

"A cheaper regression guard, which I ran: `se(att_i)` on a one-straddler panel must be close to `se(att_i)` on the same panel with that straddle removed, not 12% below it (A2 vs A4)." The test is CONFOUNDED and so is every number derived from it (the proposal's 12.0%, section 8.4's 2.9%, round 1's 12.1%). Moving a unit's later rows from cluster A to cluster B changes the nesting regime AND both clusters' contents, and the second effect alone changes the between-cluster variance of att_i. Measured size of the confound: on my k = 3 panel, b123 re-identifies 97 of the 100 units - exactly what the all-nest twin does for all 100 - and still sits 30% below the twin (.0959092 vs .1376333). Most of that gap cannot be the 3-unit rule difference.

"The first branch is the *unchanged* all-nesting expression, so the hot path is byte-for-byte what ships today" cited against A4/A4B/A4C bit-identity. Round 1 established that the measured build (b_p123, buildC) is a 2-branch always-offset variant, not the proposal's 3-branch conditional one. I built the 3-branch version as written and confirm the conclusion holds (runA Z0 and runC H0 bit-identical, including on the boottstat path), but the document still cites a build it does not describe.

"**Both no-regression guards hold** ... on the `bootstrap(standard)` and the `boottstat` path alike" (section 8.4). The boottstat half of that was measured on phantom arms only, which under buildC are not mixed regimes at all. The genuine-straddler boottstat arms had never been run by anyone; I ran them and the pure-regime guard does hold (H0: 0 of 49), but the mixed arms behave as above.
required_changes: Re-title the SMP-3 effect. It is not "the intended lift"; it is a change of sign and magnitude that depends on the straddler count. Replace the structural "rise" sentence with the measured dose curve: k = 40 gives +10.6% to +16.5%, k = 3 gives -6.7% to -20.0% over three seeds and both tau orderings.

Add the LOCATION evidence and the boottstat evidence to the body, not as a caveat: e(bias_boot)[att_i]/se moves away from zero in 10 of 10 arms by a factor of 2.5-6; under boottstat att's own p-value and interval move at k = 3; at k = 40 the bias-corrected family is withheld for att_i and the displayed studentized interval's lower bound exceeds the point estimate.

Withdraw the clean-panel / straddler-removed comparison as the yardstick, or run a design in which the cluster composition is held fixed. As it stands the proposal's central quantitative claim rests on a comparison that cannot separate the rule from the composition.

Do not resubmit without a coverage simulation on a mixed-regime design, before and after, for att_i and for att under boottstat. The proposal already names this as the missing evidence (section 8.6) and my results make it decisive rather than nice-to-have: SMP-3's claimed benefit reverses sign at realistic straddler counts while its cost - a displaced replicate distribution and, on the studentized path, an interval that can leave the point estimate - is consistent in sign everywhere I measured.

Keep round 1's required changes 3, 4 and 5 (name sthlp:1240 and sthlp:1274 - both verified present and both made false by SMP-3; state that the replicate estimand's unit weighting becomes unit-dependent within a replication; record that e(boot_reid) == 0 with e(boot_nstraddle) > 0 becomes unreachable once SMP-3 ships).
If the author wants the disclosure without the method change, SMP-4 with a corrected guard is the better bet on this evidence and the proposal should say so.
proposals.reasoning: The mechanics are sound: bit-identical on both pure regimes including under boottstat, no P7 abort on a genuine mixed code space (the gap the proposal itself flagged as the priority check and which nobody had actually tested - every previous boottstat arm was clean or phantom), and the blast radius is what is claimed on the plain path. But the substantive case collapses under measurement. The proposal's single quantitative claim - that se(att_i) rises back toward the straddler-free value - is falsified in 6 of 6 runs at a realistic straddler count, where it falls by 6.7-20.0%; the yardstick it is measured against is confounded by cluster composition by an amount comparable to the claimed effect; the replicate distribution's centre moves away from zero in 10 of 10 arms rather than in a sign that depends on the design; and on the boottstat path it changes att's own reported inference and can withhold the bias-corrected family while displaying an interval that does not contain the point estimate. DONT_SHIP is not a claim that the shipped global rule is right - it plainly is not, and the code's own comment says why - but no edit to this document turns this evidence into a case for adopting SMP-3. It needs a coverage simulation before it is a proposal at all.

proposals.which_quantities_move: No posted number moves - but as written the edit does not produce numbers at all. Measured on a clean 900-row panel, `att att_i cluster(ind) bootstrap(standard) reps(4) rseed(4242) bootdf(clusters)`: build b14 (SMP-1 + SMP-4(a) exactly as written) returns rc 0 -> 198 with "invalid syntax", printed twice, AFTER the replication loop has completed. Build b14ok (the same edit with `if "`wdb_nstrad'" == "" local wdb_nstrad .` inserted before the post) returns rc 0 and posts e(boot_reid) = 1 and e(boot_nstraddle) = . with nothing else changed. With SMP-3 also applied, round 1 measured b1234 vs b123 across four arms as numerically identical with only the two new scalars added; I did not re-run that and accept it.
falsified_claims: ROUND 1'S OWN PROPOSED FIX IS BROKEN, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS ROUND. Round 1's required change reads: "the shell hunk should still be written defensively (e.g. `ereturn scalar boot_nstraddle = `=cond(\"`wdb_nstrad'\"==\"\", ., `wdb_nstrad')'`) so an empty macro can never abort a completed run." I built exactly that (probes/rev2-SMP/b14r1) and ran it: rc 0 -> 198, "invalid syntax" printed twice, identical to the unfixed build. Mechanism, isolated in all three logs: with an empty macro the expression is `cond("" == "", ., )` - an empty THIRD argument - which Stata rejects during macro expansion, prints "invalid syntax", and expands to NOTHING, so the statement becomes `ereturn scalar boot_nstraddle = ` -> r(198). A ruling table built from round 1's text would ship the identical defect. The correct guard is the plain form, measured working in b14ok.

"Risk: none. Moves reported numbers: NO" and "This is the cheapest proposal here and I would ship it whatever happens to SMP-3." Confirmed false, independently of round 1: build b14 aborts an ordinary clean clustered bootstrap(standard) run with r(198) after the user has paid the full replication cost, because `wdb_nstrad' is c_local'd to the shell only by SMP-3 hunk (a) - and the proposal's own ship order puts SMP-3 last.

The fallback caution's "`bootstrap()` standard errors for `att` and for the ame family are unaffected." Round 1 falsified the ame half (se(ame_i) +15.44% on their contreat arm C2). I add the att half on the studentized path: under boottstat with 3 genuine straddlers in 100 units, att's reported p-value moves 0.400 -> 0.300 and its 95% interval moves [-.17109913, .97414421] -> [-.09520187, .96837311]. The honest split is observation-weighted (att, ame) unaffected in the bootstrap standard error column, cell-weighted (att_i, att_it, att_itime, ame_i) affected, and under boottstat every column's interval and p-value affected.

The fallback caution's "measured at 10-14% on panels where only one unit straddles", shipped as user-facing text. The document's own section 8.4 measured 2.9% on that configuration; my clean same-panel measurement at k = 3 gives -6.7% to -20.0%, i.e. the OPPOSITE sign from what the caution implies about which way the shipped rule errs relative to the alternative. No single signed range can be quoted.

"three sthlp sentences" / "3 sthlp sentences". Round 1's sthlp:1240 and sthlp:1274 are both real (verified: ":1240 ... a cluster finer than {it:i} simply resamples inside the cohort"; ":1274 ... finer than {it:i} or cross-cuts it the units are kept whole, the cell count does not grow"). Five sites, and a sixth sentence inside :532 about the parse-time two-cluster refusal (see SMP-1).

Round 1's `cond("`x'"=="", ., `x')` form reproduces the r(198) exactly (b14r1).

Keep round 1's structural fix as well: either gate SMP-4(a) on SMP-3 shipping, or give SMP-4 its own `local wdb_nstrad 0` initialisation plus the gegen tag + count and a `c_local wdb_nstrad `wdb_nstrad'' OUTSIDE the reid/clus conditional in wooldid_bootrun. Say that the omitted component is design-dependent and name e(boot_nstraddle) as the way to see the configuration, not a number.

Fix the caution's scope sentence to the three-way split: observation-weighted estimands (att, ame) unaffected in the bootstrap standard error; cell-weighted ones (att_i, att_it, att_itime, ame_i) affected; and under boottstat every column's interval and p-value affected, because the studentization denominator is per-replication.
Add sthlp:1240 and sthlp:1274 to the list of sites, and the :532 sentence about the parse-time two-cluster refusal from SMP-1's list.

Drop the sentence "Without SMP-3, `e(boot_nstraddle) > 0` and `e(boot_reid) == 0` is precisely the configuration FCM-1 and FCW-01 describe": unreachable in both worlds, as round 1 showed (b1234 reports e(boot_reid) = 1 on both straddler arms; without SMP-3 the edit errors).
proposals.reasoning: This is the proposal that fails on contact and the one where round 1's remedy also fails on contact. I reproduced the r(198) on an exactly-as-written build and then built round 1's own recommended guard and got the identical r(198), with the mechanism isolated (an empty third argument to cond() expands to nothing, not to a missing value). The working form is a one-line `if ... local ... .` before the post, measured rc 0 with e(boot_reid) = 1 and e(boot_nstraddle) = . posted. Beyond the packaging, two of the caution's user-facing sentences are wrong: the ame exemption (round 1) and the att exemption on the studentized path (mine), and the shipped "10-14%" figure cannot even be given a consistent sign once a realistic straddler count is measured. CHANGES rather than DONT_SHIP because the content - two scalars and a disclosure caution - is exactly right and is the better bet if SMP-3 is declined; it just cannot ship in the form or the order the document gives.
